profile.name: Eswaran S
profile.title: Security Operations Analyst
profile.tagline: Building security tooling, investigating systems, and automating analysis.
profile.shortBio: Cybersecurity fresher specializing in SOC operations, SIEM detection engineering, log analysis, and security automation.

about.summary: Cyber security fresher with hands-on experience in SIEM (Wazuh, Splunk, Sumo Logic), log analysis, incident triage, and detection rule engineering through an internship at HTC Global Services and a self-built SOC home lab. Completed the TryHackMe SOC Level 1 path; demonstrated threat detection and alert investigation skills via CTF placements including a TCS HackQuest interview offer and a PEC CTF Top 5 finish.
about.objective: Seeking an L1 SOC Analyst role to contribute practical skills in security monitoring, false positive triage, IOC identification, and MITRE ATT&CK-mapped threat response.
careerHighlights: Earned TCS HackQuest interview offer through 2 CTF elimination rounds
Secured 5th place in PEC Capture The Flag out of 100+ participants
Architected 3-node virtual SOC home lab with sub-30s MTTD

currentFocus: Expanding Cloud Knowledge coverage in AWS
Deepening Splunk SPL and detection rule engineering
Practicing SOC Environment in Cloud AWS
Advancing through defensive security courses on Udemy and TryHackMe

experience.summary: Structured 10-month training programme covering six cybersecurity domains, Also learnt about SOC operations in Sumo Logic SIEM.
responsibilities: Built foundational SOC operations competency across 6 cybersecurity domains - Windows/Linux administration, network protocol analysis, SIEM concepts, incident response lifecycle, and DFIR - over a 10-month structured training programme.

Monitored and investigated security events using Sumo Logic SIEM - configured log collection pipelines, authored search queries, and built dashboards to surface anomalous authentication and lateral movement indicators across training environments.

Detected and analysed security event categories - including failed logon patterns, suspicious process creation, and network anomalies - by correlating Wireshark packet captures, Sysmon telemetry, and Windows Event Log data for alert investigation and false positive triage.

Executed network reconnaissance and vulnerability assessment using Nmap and Metasploit in adversarial simulation exercises, mapping identified attack techniques to MITRE ATT&CK TTPs to strengthen defensive detection strategies.
outcomes: Completed 10-month structured program covering 6 cybersecurity domains
Configured Sumo Logic log pipelines and alert triage dashboards

projects.name: Mini SOC Lab
projects.subtitle: 3-Node Security Operations Home Lab
projects.summary: Architected and operated a 3-node SOC home lab simulating real-world threat detection, incident triage, and alert escalation workflows end-to-end.
projects.description: A self-engineered security operations environment built to practice full-cycle SOC workflows. A Debian-based SIEM node ingests telemetry from two Windows 11 endpoints virtualised on VMware, while a Kali Linux attacker host launches adversarial simulations. Custom detection rules surface attacks with sub-30-second mean time to detect.
projects.problem: Real SOC environments cannot be safely used for learning. Gaining hands-on experience with end-to-end detection, triage, and escalation workflows requires a personal lab that mirrors production telemetry sources without exposing production systems.
projects.solution: Build a self-contained virtual network where a SIEM (Wazuh/Splunk) collects Windows Event Log and Sysmon telemetry from monitored endpoints, while a Kali attacker runs MITRE ATT&CK-mapped TTPs. Engineer custom detection rules, trigger real-time alerts, and iterate detection coverage across multiple attack stages.
projects.role: Sole builder - architecture, detection engineering, adversarial simulation, and analysis.
features: Custom detection rules for SSH brute-force and suspicious process creation
Real-time alerting with sub-30-second mean time to detect
MITRE ATT&CK-mapped attack scenarios for detection validation
highlights: End-to-end threat detection, triage, and escalation workflow
Iterative expansion of MITRE ATT&CK coverage
challenges: Configuring log ingestion pipelines without dropping Sysmon telemetry
Tuning false positives in SSH brute force detection rules
lessons: Importance of granular Windows Event Log auditing policies
Proper MITRE ATT&CK mapping for alert validation

projects.name: Web VAPT Document Automation Tool
projects.subtitle: Penetration Testing Report Platform
projects.summary: Web-based automation platform streamlining VAPT documentation, release management, and report exchange workflows for penetration testing engagements.
projects.description: A web application that automates the creation, editing, export, and secure exchange of VAPT (Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing) reports. Built with JWT authentication and role-based access control, then hardened through direct security testing of authentication flows, authorisation, and REST API access control.
projects.problem: Manual VAPT reporting is time-consuming and error-prone. Engagement teams need a secure, auditable way to create, manage, and exchange pentest reports across release cycles.
projects.solution: Build a web platform with automated report creation, editing, export, and email workflows, fronted by JWT auth and RBAC. Harden the platform by testing REST API endpoints for authentication, authorisation, and access control vulnerabilities, remediating discovered misconfigurations.
projects.role: Developer - feature build, security testing, and remediation.
features: JWT-based authentication and role-based access control
Automated VAPT report creation, editing, and export
Security-tested authentication, authorisation, and access control flows
highlights: Reduced manual reporting effort across release workflows
Identified and remediated security misconfigurations in REST API endpoints
Validated all authentication flows through security testing
challenges: Securing REST endpoints against unauthorized privilege escalation
lessons: Importance of robust JWT validation and strict RBAC controls

projects.name: AISA
projects.subtitle: AI Security Operations Analyst
projects.summary: An agentic AI security analyst concept for investigating SOC alerts and invoking tools instead of relying on unsupported model guesses.
projects.description: AISA explores local LLM-driven SOC investigation with structured alert inputs, tool calling, and automated investigation reports.
projects.problem: SOC analysts face high alert volumes and context switching across SIEM and security tools during initial alert triage and investigation.
projects.solution: Built an agentic AI security assistant using local LLMs and LangGraph that ingests Splunk alerts, determines required triage actions, and generates investigation findings.
projects.role: Sole Developer - agent architecture, prompt/tool engineering, and SIEM integration.
features: Tool-oriented investigation workflows with local LLM
Automated incident report and recommendation generation
highlights: Explored local LLM agent execution without sending sensitive log data externally
Automated multi-step SOC alert investigation logic
challenges: Preventing hallucinated triage steps by constraining model tool execution
lessons: Structured schema-driven tool calling improves AI investigation reliability

projects.name: ML-UEBA
projects.subtitle: Log Anomaly Detection Engine
projects.summary: Machine-learning experimentation for user/entity behavior analytics and anomalous log activity detection.
projects.description: Machine-learning experimentation for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) to identify anomalous activity patterns across security logs.
projects.problem: Static signature rules struggle to detect novel insider threats and subtle behavioral shifts in enterprise environments.
projects.solution: Developed ML models to analyze baseline behavior patterns across system and authentication logs to flag statistical outliers for analyst review.
projects.role: Developer - data preprocessing, model evaluation, and log analysis.
highlights: Applied machine learning methods to identify anomalous log entries
challenges: Filtering noisy background event logs prior to model training
lessons: Feature engineering is crucial for log anomaly detection performance

projects.name: AWS SOC Environment
projects.subtitle: Cloud Security Monitoring Lab
projects.summary: A hands-on AWS lab using EC2 hosts, VPC networking, Terraform, and Splunk to build and troubleshoot a cloud security monitoring environment.
projects.description: A cloud security monitoring lab provisioned using Terraform in AWS. Features Splunk SIEM ingesting logs from multi-OS endpoints (Windows & Debian) across customized VPC subnets.
projects.problem: Deploying and managing SIEM forwarders and log ingestion pipelines across cloud infrastructure requires practical cloud networking and IaC expertise.
projects.solution: Architected an automated AWS lab topology via Terraform, deploying EC2 instances, configuring security groups, and setting up Splunk Universal Forwarders for cloud telemetry collection.
projects.role: Sole builder - cloud infrastructure, IaC automation, SIEM forwarder configuration.
features: Splunk SIEM server with Universal Forwarders on EC2
Windows and Linux log ingestion experimentation
highlights: Automated lab provisioning using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform)
Configured end-to-end cloud SIEM log pipeline
challenges: Troubleshooting Splunk Universal Forwarder TCP 9997 connectivity across VPC subnets
lessons: Infrastructure as Code streamlines consistent lab replication in AWS
